dimensions.summary: The thin-film optics has the right building blocks: Snell's law with cos(theta_t), exact s/p Fresnel (not Schlick), the Airy formula (algebraically correct) and a single sRGB encode. One sign error makes every rendered interference color wrong. All four implementations add a pi (lambda/2) phase shift and then feed it into an Airy formula that already contains that shift through r21 = -r12. This turns sin^2(delta/2) into cos^2(delta/2). I confirmed numerically that code(d) equals exact(d + lambda/(4 n cos theta_t)) to within 6e-16, and that the code's reflectance anti-correlates with the true reflectance (r = -0.999). Near d=0 the film renders at maximum brightness instead of as black film. Measured against a 1 nm CIE 1931 x D65 reference, the color error is DeltaE76 = 27-97 over 30-800 nm. The bug came in with commit 4fef328, when the correct two-beam form (1+cos(phi))/2 was replaced. A hard 30 nm black cutoff in the shader and a d<=0 guard on the CPU side hide it, and the tests only check value ranges. Secondary color-pipeline issues: the normal-incidence row of the 8-bit linear LUT holds only 9 levels, so colors posterize. The CIE Gaussian fit drops the asymmetric sigmas of Wyman 2013, so the white point comes out orange (1, 0.76, 0.43). The 7-sample spectral integration aliases above about 1.1 um (DeltaE 19-31). Separately, the procedural drainage gradient in the shader is upside down (thinnest at the bottom).
confirmed_correct: Snell's law correct with n_film relative to air in all paths: interference.rs:212-213 `(self.refractive_index_medium / self.refractive_index_film) * sin_theta_incident`; interference_lut.rs:98 `let sin_theta_t = sin_theta_i / n_film;`; bubble.wgsl:341; bubble_instanced.wgsl:127. cos(theta_t), the refracted angle, not cos(theta_i), is used in the optical path: interference.rs:243-244, interference_lut.rs:61, bubble.wgsl:453, bubble_instanced.wgsl:201.

Fresnel is the full s/p form, not Schlick, and is applied at the external air->film angle together with theta_t: interference.rs:295-303, interference_lut.rs:103-120, bubble.wgsl:348-373. F0 = ((n-1)/(n+1))^2 = 0.020059 at normal incidence, checked numerically. Polarizations are averaged for unpolarized light; see optics-07 for the order of operations. For a symmetric air/film/air slab, using a single R for both interfaces (Stokes r21 = -r12) is valid.

Airy algebra is correct and the CPU and GPU forms agree: 2R(1-cos)/(1+R^2-2R cos) (interference.rs:357-359) is identical to F sin^2/(1+F sin^2) with F=4R/(1-R)^2 (bubble.wgsl:378-398, interference_lut.rs:123-133). With the +pi removed, it matches the exact complex-amplitude slab reflectance to 6e-16 at normal incidence (airy_check.py [2]). Only the phase argument is wrong (optics-01).

Two-beam vs Airy: the code uses full Airy, which is justified. The two-beam approximation would differ from exact by 1.98% of peak at normal incidence, 9.9% at cos=0.5 and 16.5% at cos=0.3 (airy_check.py [2]).

sRGB transfer is applied exactly once end-to-end: the LUT is linear Rgba8Unorm (pipeline.rs:411), the shader outputs linear values (bubble.wgsl:544), the surface prefers an sRGB format (pipeline.rs:335-340, `.find(|f| f.is_srgb())`), headless renders to Rgba8UnormSrgb (headless.rs:85), and screenshot readback does not re-encode (frame_exporter.rs:285-301). The CPU linear_to_srgb uses the correct IEC 61966-2-1 constants (interference.rs:43-49) but is only in the unused CPU path.
XYZ->linear sRGB matrix is the standard D65 matrix (interference_lut.rs:155-159, bubble.wgsl:415-421).
The LUT is regenerated when the refractive index changes (pipeline.rs:863-894), and the refractive index is validated in [1,3] (config.rs:413-418).
f32 phase precision is adequate: the maximum argument is 2pi*2*1.33*2000/400 = 84 rad, giving about 1e-5 absolute sin error in f32.

CPU/GPU consistency: interference_lut.rs, bubble.wgsl:442-483 (legacy) and bubble_instanced.wgsl:191-219 implement identical math, apart from 8-bit LUT quantization. The CPU InterferenceCalculator (3 wavelengths, no CMF, sRGB-encoded, no x4) is a different model, but it is only re-exported (physics/mod.rs:22) and not used for rendering. It shares the same +pi bug, which the d<=0 guard at interference.rs:331 hides.

dimensions.summary: Neither drainage solver gives physically meaningful output at default settings. The CPU solver (drainage.rs) uses explicit Euler, and its frame dt is neither clamped nor sub-stepped. At the default time_scale of 100 and 60 fps it steps dt = 1.67 s, but the stable limit at the ring next to the pole is 0.115 s. A faithful numpy replica blows up near both poles within about 25 frames, with spikes up to 1.56e4 nm and rings of zeros. The GPU solver is a provable no-op: params.dt is never written (the setters have no callers), so every sub-step uses 1 ms. That increment is 0.007 ulp of a 500 nm f32 value, and a uniform start gives zero Laplacian and zero surfactant gradient, so the thickness buffer that branched flow and caustics read stays at exactly 500 nm forever. The PDE in both solvers is the same and has the wrong units and the wrong form. The gravity term -rho*g*h^3/(3*eta)*sin(theta) is in m^2/s (a flux, not its divergence) and is a mass sink everywhere; it treats both hemispheres the same, so the bottom never thickens and the top pole never thins, the opposite of the correct conservative lubrication form. The 'Monier 0.85 TFE ratio' is applied as an unbounded exponential decay that turns the film black and goes negative for dt > 13.3 s. The spherical Laplacian, periodic phi wrap, 256x128 grid constants, struct layout and the ping-pong bind groups are all correct. The docs describing the drainage equation, pole handling, roadmap status and TFE naming are stale or dimensionally wrong.

dimensions.summary: I checked the branched-flow ray optics and the caustics module against first-principles derivations and Python replicas of the WGSL kernels. Nothing ran on a GPU; all scripts are in scratchpad/branched/. Several pieces are correct. Zero-force rays follow exact great circles (error 1.9e-15), kick-plus-renormalize gives dT/ds = k·F⊥ to first order, and the scatterer force, frame handedness, ×64/÷64 encoding, u32 headroom and prefix-sum hash all check out. The serious problems are in units and scaling, not the integrator. The thickness buffer holds metres and thickness_scale is never applied, so the GRIN term bends rays by only about 2e-4°: every visible branch comes from the scatterers, and the 'GRIN bending' slider actually scales the particle force. The caustics compute has the same unit bug and outputs a constant 2.0 everywhere. With the feature enabled, the default patch view lights only about 4-6% of the patch. The causes are a chord-for-gnomonic spawn offset, a patch centre 90° from the entry point, and the adaptive step sitting at its 0.3 floor in 97-99% of steps, which also contradicts the new working-tree comments. Issue #35 (temporal accumulation) is effectively implemented by the 0.85 fade. It adds no sampling density, though, because ray seeds do not change between frames.
confirmed_correct: Zero-force rays are exact great circles: the gnomonic chart maps straight lines to geodesics. Replica max |p·n_plane| = 1.9e-15 over 5 rays × 2000 steps (branched_flow_compute.wgsl:494, 542).

Kick then renormalize implements the ray-optics equation dT/ds = k·F⊥ to first order: normalize(v + kF dt) = v + k dt (F - (F·v)v) + O(dt²), so the tangential force is correctly removed (branched_flow_compute.wgsl:530-539).

The scatterer force equals -∇V for V = V0·exp(-r²/2σ²): 2·inv_sigma_sq = 1/σ², delta points from the scatterer to the ray, and positive strength repels (branched_flow_compute.wgsl:303-317; branched_flow.rs:222).
Scatterer cutoff r² > 4.5/inv_sigma_sq equals r > 3σ, consistent between scatterer_force and scatterer_in_range (branched_flow_compute.wgsl:309, 326).

The tangent frame (t1, t2, E) is orthonormal and right-handed (t1 × t2 = E), and φ̂ = (-n.z, 0, n.x)/|xz| = ∂P/∂φ normalized while n × φ̂ = (cosθcosφ, -sinθ, cosθsinφ) = ∂P/∂θ, consistent with the u→φ and v→θ sign conventions (branched_flow_compute.wgsl:428-433, 150-153).
The initial vel_2d is unit length and tangent: beam_dir is projected onto the tangent plane, then normalized in the frame (branched_flow_compute.wgsl:425, 443-447).
The ×64 encode matches the ÷64 decode (branched_flow_compute.wgsl:388; bubble.wgsl:272-275), and both use the same u·(W−1) texel mapping (wgsl:369; bubble.wgsl:246).

u32 overflow headroom: the worst case of every ray-step landing in one pixel at 0.85-fade steady state is 3.1e8 (8192×200) and 2.5e9 (UI max 65536×200), both below 4.29e9. ray_steps is not exposed in the UI (ui_state.rs:467 exposes only num_rays). The realistic peak is ~3.4e4 (estimated).
The 0.85 fade at branched_flow_compute.wgsl:566-569 is temporal accumulation (#35 effectively implemented), and truncation guarantees decay to 0.
The v-mapping v·(H−1) of the thickness sampler matches the drainage grid θ_j = jπ/(H−1) (branched_flow_compute.wgsl:243; drainage.wgsl:92, 96).

The spatial hash is correct at the default radius: the CPU sort key and prefix sum match the GPU cell indexing and clamping, offsets[100] = N, and scatterer padding to MAX_SCATTERERS means stale tail entries are never read (branched_flow.rs:641-671; branched_flow_compute.wgsl:101-105, 345-353).

The patch-local UV remap is identical in compute and fragment (branched_flow_compute.wgsl:205-210; bubble.wgsl:293-302), and the patch-local texels are square at the equator: 1.99 rad/512 ≈ 0.993 rad/256 ≈ 0.0039 rad.

Pole handling does not distort physics at defaults: reach is atan(2.5) = 68.2° from an equatorial entry, so sinθ ≥ 0.371 > 0.15 and the taper is inactive. In general the taper affects only sinθ < 0.15, which is 1.1% of the sphere area (branched_flow_compute.wgsl:279-281).
The GRIN sign is right: rays bend toward +∇h, i.e. thicker film, consistent with a TE0 n_eff that increases monotonically with d (branched_flow_compute.wgsl:499, 530; check_neff.py).
Struct layout: BranchedFlowParams is 112 bytes with tested offsets matching the WGSL, and ScattererGPU is 16 bytes (branched_flow.rs:761-790, 896-903).
open_questions: The CLAUDE.md note that a loop-body change froze the GPU is unexplained. On WSLg llvmpipe (#38), a longer compute dispatch may trip the compositor watchdog. Fixes that add per-step work (3D exp-map integration, turning-angle step criterion, thickness_scale in the helpers) should be tested with a reduced num_rays first.

All branched-flow numbers come from a Python float64/f32 replica of the WGSL, not from GPU runs. Exact hash-collision counts may differ in the low bits on real GPU f32 (FMA). The patch-coverage result (4-6%) should be confirmed visually in the app with branched flow and GPU drainage enabled.
For the drainage auditor: gpu_drainage.rs:501-505 current_buffer() returns the previous substep's buffer (see branched-12). Please confirm it does not affect drainage-internal consumers.

#36 (shared-memory deposits) and #37 (workgroup tuning): the replica shows deposits concentrated in ~4% of texels, a peak of ~79 per texel per frame (estimated), so atomic contention is likely hot-spotted. Worth measuring on real hardware before and after #36.

After the unit fix (branched-01), should GRIN be calibrated physically (bend ≈ 0.02-0.04 with h in µm, giving weak bending from the drainage profile) or kept artistic? The answer decides whether #39 (noise in compute) is the main source of branching.

dimensions.summary: Geometry/camera math is mostly right: UV-sphere seams and poles, ellipsoid normals, sphere-sphere intersection radius, the Rodrigues rotation, look_at_rh plus perspective_rh with 0..1 depth, the pitch clamp and the resize aspect guard all check out. So do the core samplers (log-normal mu, Schulz-Flory k/theta, Marsaglia-Tsang, Box-Muller, xorshift64). The most user-visible defect is a 180-degree longitude mismatch: the SpherePatch mesh is built with phi=2*pi*u, but both shaders use u=(atan2(z,x)+pi)/2pi. In the default-on patch view, none of the 1089 patch vertices fall inside the shader's patch window, so no branched flow is drawn there; full-sphere mode is not affected. A faithful Python re-implementation of FoamSimulator::step shows the foam dynamics are driven by the velocity clamp, not by the forces. Explicit Stokes drag (water viscosity, film-only mass, k/m=3/R) is unstable for R<22 mm at 60 fps. With the default cluster, every bubble jitters 1.67 mm per frame at the 0.1 m/s clamp indefinitely. Buoyancy drops the enclosed-air mass, so gravity is clamped to zero for R>1.25 mm. The foam geometry contradicts the module's own Plateau/Young-Laplace claims: there is no 120-degree enforcement, the contact equilibrium is at d~0.95(Ra+Rb) instead of sqrt(Ra^2+Rb^2-RaRb), and the shared-wall radius is half the physical value and bulges into the wrong (smaller) bubble. The foam shaders also carry the project-wide Airy +pi double count, and wall.wgsl uses the transmission form as its reflected colour. Smaller items: clamped (not truncated) size distributions, a non-HCP 'HCP' lattice, pole-clustered random spawning, an instanced-normal correction that cancels itself, non-volume-conserving deformation with dead Bond-number code, and several stale docs.

dimensions.summary: CPU-side per-frame cost is small. A standalone rustc replica, timed min-of-N at load avg 16 on 8 cores, puts the per-frame branched-flow scatterer perturbation + sort + prefix-sum at 17 us for n=400 (94 us for n=2048). The per-frame create_bind_group costs an estimated few-to-tens of us, and foam O(n^2) is capped at 30 bubbles by the UI. None of these show up against a 16.7 ms frame. The real risks in the audited files are two wgpu validation panics and some wrong time-stepping. (1) Changing MSAA rebuilds only the bubble pipeline: the foam/wall/caustic pipelines keep sample count 4, so the app panics. (2) The GpuProfiler records a copy into a buffer whose map may still be pending, which panics on real GPUs with TIMESTAMP_QUERY whenever the GPU lags a frame; this cannot be seen on WSLg. (3) GPU drainage never uploads its computed step dt, so time_scale is dead and the displayed clock is 167x off at 60 fps. (4) CPU drainage takes one explicit-Euler step of dt = frame_dt*100, about 14x over the polar phi-diffusion stability limit; this was reproduced in a Rust replica and a numpy port. dimensions.summary: GPU-optimization audit of the branched-flow, drainage, caustic and render passes, done by code reading, reading the wgpu 24.0.5 sources, and a numpy copy of branched_flow_compute.wgsl main() at default parameters (scratchpad/gpuperf/ray_replica.py, divergence.py, f32_drainage.py, bufidx.py). No GPU timings were taken. Every speedup figure is an estimate. On this WSL machine the defaults hit three problems: 1) the scatterer loop costs about 170 scatterer evaluations per ray-step; 2) fixed-point deposits lose 57% of their energy to truncation; 3) the GRIN/drainage path does no useful work, because the drainage dt is never uploaded and f32 rounding freezes the thickness field. Two latent crash bugs in GpuProfiler will switch on as soon as the app runs on an adapter that supports timestamps. #38 is partly refuted: vulkaninfo shows the RTX 3070 Ti Laptop GPU through Mesa Dozen. Ranked by expected speedup on a real discrete GPU (all estimated): (1) compute the per-frame force field once instead of summing scatterers per ray-step, about 10x less per-step work; (2) limit each step by turning angle instead of the pinned 0.3x clamp, about 2.6x fewer steps for the same path; (3) on discrete GPUs, raise rays back toward 32K, which restores quality at little cost because 8K rays leave the GPU mostly idle; (4) drop the dead GRIN loads and frozen drainage passes, or fix the physics; (5) switch the foam shader to the LUT (matters only on llvmpipe); (6) atomics and subgroups last, about 0.15 ms. #35 is effectively done, #36 is not viable as written, and #37 is the wrong lever.

Pass ordering in one command encoder is correct: drainage -> caustic -> BF clear -> BF trace -> render (pipeline.rs:1407-1546). wgpu inserts the storage-buffer barriers between passes, so the fade runs before deposits and the fragment shader reads the finished buffer.
The branched-flow bind group is rebuilt each frame with the drainage buffer (pipeline.rs:1424-1428), which prevents a fixed stale binding. The returned buffer is one sub-step old; see gpuperf-03.

The spatial-hash sort key and prefix sum on the CPU (branched_flow.rs:641-658) use the same clamp-then-truncate cell function as the shader's uv_to_grid_cell (branched_flow_compute.wgsl:101-105), so the cell_offsets ranges are consistent.

The trace kernel has no workgroupBarrier or storageBarrier, so there is no barrier-under-divergence hazard (branched_flow_compute.wgsl:405-553). With the defaults the loop trip count is uniform (both breaks are dead: 0.999^200 = 0.82; travel 0.3 is far below 2.5), and the scatterer inner loop has warp efficiency 0.998 in the replica.
Scaling the deposit by step_factor (branched_flow_compute.wgsl:523,526) correctly weights deposited energy by path length.
u32 fixed-point atomics are the right portable choice: SHADER_FLOAT32_ATOMIC is Vulkan-extension or Metal only (wgpu-types-24.0.0 lib.rs:499-508), so it is unavailable on DX12 and Dozen.
The clear and fade pass is cheap on hardware: 131K threads, about 1 MiB read+write per frame (branched_flow_compute.wgsl:559-570), estimated microseconds.
GPU struct sizes and offsets are tested against WGSL (branched_flow.rs:761-790; gpu_drainage.rs:528-556).

On this machine, Mesa 26.0.5 'Dozen' (dzn) already exposes the RTX 3070 Ti Laptop GPU as a Vulkan 1.2 discrete adapter, measured with vulkaninfo. wgpu-hal 24 (and still v30.0.1) hides any adapter whose conformanceVersion.major is 0 unless InstanceFlags::ALLOW_UNDERLYING_NONCOMPLIANT_ADAPTER is set. A small code change (flags with_env plus PowerPreference::HighPerformance) is the cheapest route to hardware acceleration; a native Windows build is the robust fallback. While building the SOTA comparisons I re-derived several math defects that matter more than any SOTA gap: (1) the Airy formula is given an extra +pi phase, which inverts every interference fringe (cross-dimension, high); (2) the LUT uses 7 wavelengths and a CIE fit with the wrong (symmetric) sigmas; (3) the GPU drainage dt never reaches the shader, so the thickness field stays essentially uniform, and wiring dt naively would break the explicit stability limit at the poles. Literature: keep the ray model for branched flow (Patsyk 2022 shows the main branches are ray caustics), but bend rays with grad n_eff(d), not grad d. The Huang 2020 reduced model is the SOTA that fits the existing lat-long grid.

findings.title: pi phase shift counted twice in the Airy formula inverts every interference fringe (black film renders at maximum brightness)
findings.claim: The live render path (the interference_lut.rs LUT, sampled by bubble.wgsl) and the instanced foam path both evaluate Airy reflectance F sin^2(phi/2)/(1+F sin^2(phi/2)) with phi = 4 pi n d cos(theta_t)/lambda + pi. The Airy formula already contains the reflection phase flip, so the extra +pi turns sin^2(delta/2) into cos^2(delta/2). Every bright fringe becomes dark and vice versa, and as d->0 the film shows maximum reflectance 4R/(1+R)^2 = 0.0771 instead of 0. Same bug at bubble_instanced.wgsl:208, bubble.wgsl:464 (legacy function the LUT mirrors) and interference.rs:248 (CPU, + lambda/2 added to the OPD before the Airy formula at :357-359).
findings.derivation: Air(1)/film(n)/air(1). Interface amplitudes: r12 = r (negative at normal incidence, this is the pi flip), r23 = r21 = -r (Stokes), t12 t21 = 1 - r^2. Summing all reflected beams: r_tot = [r12 + r23 e^{i delta}]/[1 + r12 r23 e^{i delta}] = r(1 - e^{i delta})/(1 - r^2 e^{i delta}), with delta = 4 pi n d cos(theta_t)/lambda (geometric round-trip phase only). |r_tot|^2 = R(2 - 2cos delta)/(1 + R^2 - 2R cos delta) = F sin^2(delta/2)/(1 + F sin^2(delta/2)), F = 4R/(1-R)^2. The sign flip between r12 and r23 is already in this formula. Adding another pi gives sin^2((delta+pi)/2) = cos^2(delta/2). The two-beam form (1+cos(delta+pi))/2 = sin^2(delta/2) that the code used before commit 4fef328 was correct. That commit swapped `0.5*(1+cos(phase))` for `airy_interference(phase)` and kept the +pi (git show 4fef328, bubble.wgsl hunk). The repo's own references/Glassner_2000_Soap_Bubbles_Part2_summary.md:48 gives I_r = 4 I_i R_f sin^2(2 pi w eta cos theta_t/lambda), the sin^2 form. Numeric check (scratchpad/optics/airy_check.py, exact per-polarization slab via complex amplitudes): n=1.33, lambda=550, cos=1: d=0.5 nm exact 0.00000, code 0.07711 (CPU 0.07711); d=30 nm exact 0.0159, code 0.0631; d=100 nm exact 0.0769 (first-order max), code 0.0002. max|code(d) - exact(d + lambda/(4n))| = 5.7e-16 over d in [0,1500] nm, a wavelength-dependent shift of 84.6/103.4/122.2 nm at 450/550/650. corr(code, exact) = -0.9992 (cos=1), -0.986 (cos=0.5), -0.93 (cos=0.3). With the +pi removed, max|code - exact| = 5.7e-16 at normal incidence. DeltaE76 = 27.7, 42.1, 38.5, 34.6, 64.1, 64.9, 62.5, 52.9, 97.0, 62.9, 86.0, 90.8, 66.1, 57.1 at d = 50, 80, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 400, 450, 500, 600, 700, 800 nm. Every row in 30-800 nm has a large error. The code shows roughly the complementary color sequence: code ~ F - exact, max deviation 6e-3.

findings.title: Interference LUT stored as linear Rgba8Unorm: only 9 of 255 levels used at normal incidence, so colors posterize
findings.claim: The LUT stores physical reflectance-weighted XYZ->RGB values, which are tiny (max 0.0386 on the cos=1 row), as truncated 8-bit linear values. The shader then multiplies by interference_intensity=4. At normal incidence each channel therefore has only about 9 distinct output values, spaced 0.0157 apart in linear, and the first non-zero level jumps straight to sRGB8 34.
findings.derivation: I replicated generate_interference_lut (intensity=1) in color_check.py [C]. The maximum stored linear value is 0.0386 on the normal-incidence row, which is 9 of 255 levels, and 0.537 over all angles (grazing). After the x4 in bubble.wgsl:436 the step is 4/255 = 0.0157 linear. In the [D] table, every normal-incidence displayed channel value falls in the set {0,34,50,61,71,79,86,93,99,105} (sRGB8). The `as u8` cast truncates rather than rounds, a bias of -0.5 LSB.
findings.impact: Visible color banding and contouring across the bubble center, where cos(theta) is near 1 and the thickness gradient is smooth. The instanced foam shader computes the spectrum inline in f32 without this quantization, so the single-bubble and foam paths render the same thickness differently.
findings.recommendation: Store the LUT as Rgba16Float (filterable in wgpu core, 256x64x8 B = 128 KiB). Alternatively, normalize by the LUT's maximum and pass the scale in the uniform, or store it sRGB-encoded in Rgba8UnormSrgb so the hardware decodes it. Round instead of truncating. This should be done alongside optics-01, because the corrected LUT has the same dynamic range.

verification.reasoning: Verified: the LUT is written as `(rgb.clamp(0,1)*255.0) as u8` (interference_lut.rs:33), which truncates. The texture is Rgba8Unorm (pipeline.rs:411, headless.rs:163), and bubble.wgsl:436 multiplies by interference_intensity, default 4.0 (pipeline.rs:77). At normal incidence the physical reflectance tops out near 4R/(1+R)^2 = 0.077, and the code's d=0 texel works out by hand to linear RGB (0.033, 0.025, 0.014). A row maximum of about 0.0386 (9-10 levels) is therefore plausible. After x4 one LSB is 0.0157 linear, and the first non-zero level maps to sRGB8 34, which I confirmed. However, the sampler is Linear/Linear (pipeline.rs:441-442), so textureSample interpolates between adjacent texels and the displayed values are not limited to the texel-centre levels. The foam path computes inline in f32 (bubble_instanced.wgsl:191-219), so the single-bubble and foam paths do differ.
verification.corrected_claim: The 8-bit linear LUT keeps only about 9-10 code values across the whole normal-incidence row. With x4 that is a quantization step of ±0.008 linear, plus a -0.5 LSB truncation bias and flat plateaus wherever neighbouring texels share a level. Linear filtering interpolates between texels, so the output is not limited to 9 discrete values. The result is contouring and plateaus along smooth thickness gradients rather than strict 9-level posterization. Rgba16Float or a normalized/sRGB encoding with rounding fixes it.

findings.title: CIE CMF Gaussian fit mis-transcribed (asymmetric sigmas dropped), and no illuminant: a flat white reflector renders orange
findings.claim: cie_color_matching uses single-sigma Gaussians, but the Wyman-Sloan-Shirley 2013 multi-lobe fit that the coefficients come from is piecewise, with different left and right sigmas. Errors at the sample wavelengths: z(450) 1.305 vs table 1.772 (-26%), y(500) 0.4545 vs 0.323 (+41%), x(650) 0.439 vs 0.2835 (+55%), y(650) 0.184 vs 0.107 (+72%), x(700) 0.032 vs 0.0114 (2.8x). XYZ is also accumulated with equal-energy weighting and divided by 7, with no D65 illuminant, before the D65 sRGB matrix. As a result, a spectrally flat reflectance maps to linear sRGB proportional to (1, 0.761, 0.430) instead of (1,1,1). The same code is at bubble.wgsl:402-412 and bubble_instanced.wgsl:171-180.
findings.derivation: Compared against the CVRL CIE 1931 2-degree 1 nm table (color_check.py [A]). Wyman 2013 piecewise form, e.g. z = 1.217 g(437; 11.8, 36.0) + 0.681 g(459; 26.0, 13.8): at 450 nm that gives 1.7816 vs table 1.7721 (0.5%), and at 500 nm 0.2714 vs 0.2720. The code instead uses only the left sigma (11.8, 26.0) on both sides, giving 1.3047 and 0.1964. White point [B]: sum over 7 samples of the code CMFs divided by 7 gives XYZ=(0.328,0.339,0.223), which is linear sRGB normalized (1, 0.761, 0.430), an orange cast. Table CMFs with equal energy give (1, 0.728, 0.724), pink. A 1 nm D65 reference gives (1.000,1.000,1.000). Isolated error, with the phase fixed, 7 samples and no quantization, code CMF/E vs table CMF/D65: DeltaE76 = 16.3, 11.8, 12.6, 19.5, 3.9, 7.8 at d = 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 700 nm.
findings.impact: The whole palette has a systematic warm/orange cast. The thick-film limit, which should be near-white pastel, and the first-order white near 100 nm come out yellow-orange. Blues are under-weighted by about 26%.
findings.recommendation: The LUT is precomputed on the CPU, so use the tabulated CIE 1931 2-degree CMFs (5 nm, 81 rows) weighted by the D65 SPD, normalized so that the integral of y(lambda) D65(lambda) d(lambda) = 1. Minimal fix: restore the six right-side sigmas from Wyman 2013 (31.0, 26.7, 26.2 / 40.5, and 16.3 left for the y lobe 2 / 36.0, 13.8) and weight by D65.

verification.reasoning: interference_lut.rs:136-145, bubble.wgsl:402-412 and bubble_instanced.wgsl:171-180 all use one sigma per lobe. Wyman 2013 lobes are piecewise; the code keeps the left sigmas except for the y-bar 530.9 lobe, where it uses the right sigma 31.1 (left 16.3). I recomputed by hand. Code z(450) = 0.6634 + 0.6415 = 1.305, against the piecewise (sigma_right 36.0 for the 437 lobe) 1.7817 and CIE 1.7721. y(500) = 0.4546 against piecewise 0.327. x(650) = 0.4393 against piecewise 0.2847 and CIE 0.2835. Equal-energy white through the 7 code samples: sum x = 2.2977, sum y = 2.3753, sum z = 1.5636, divided by 7 = (0.328, 0.339, 0.223), matching the finding. The D65 matrix gives linear RGB (0.4305, 0.3277, 0.1852), normalized (1, 0.761, 0.430), an orange cast as claimed. There is no illuminant weighting (:81-83 divide by 7). Whether to weight by D65 is a modelling choice, but the warm cast is real. The per-thickness ΔE76 values are the finder's and were not reproduced here.

findings.title: 7-sample 50 nm spectral integration aliases: DeltaE 6.5 at the default 500 nm, 19-31 above 1 um (LUT spans 0-2000 nm, 'Thick' preset = 1200 nm)
findings.claim: The fringe period in wavelength is about lambda^2/(2 n d cos theta_t). At 50 nm spacing this falls below the Nyquist limit (period < 100 nm) at 450 nm for d > about 800 nm, and at 550 nm for d > 1137 nm. The LUT covers 0-2000 nm, the UI slider goes to 1500 nm (ui_state.rs:129), and the 'Thick' preset sets 1200 nm (ui_state.rs:154). Thick films should wash out toward white or pastel, but they render as saturated aliased colors.
findings.derivation: Fringe period at 450/550/650 nm: d=800: 95/142/199 nm; d=1000: 76/114/159; d=1500: 51/76/106; d=2000: 38/57/79 (airy_check.py [6]). To isolate the sampling error I used the correct phase, table CMFs and D65 for both, comparing the 7-sample sum with a 1 nm integral (color_check.py [E]). DeltaE76 = 3.5 (100 nm), 3.2 (300), 6.5 (500, the default base_thickness), 2.9 (800), 18.6 (1000), 21.3 (1200), 23.3 (1500), 31.1 (2000). Example at 1500 nm: reference (70,65,65), near-grey; 7-sample (86,59,29), orange. At 2000 nm: (66,65,66) vs (0,80,55).
findings.impact: Higher-order (thick) film colors are wrong and stay falsely saturated. There is also a noticeable error at the default 500 nm thickness.
findings.recommendation: The LUT is built once on the CPU, so integrate at 1-5 nm (81-401 samples x 256 x 64 texels, a few ms in Rust), with zero runtime cost. bubble_instanced.wgsl evaluates the spectrum per fragment, so switch it to sample the same LUT texture instead of the inline 7-sample loop. For a runtime analytic solution, Belcour & Barla 2017 integrate the Airy series against Gaussian sensor responses in the Fourier domain, which filters out high-order fringes.

verification.reasoning: WAVELENGTHS has 7 samples at 50 nm spacing (interference_lut.rs:52), and the LUT spans 0-2000 nm (:13). Re-derived: the term is periodic in wavenumber with period 1/(2 n d cos theta_t), so the 50 nm step aliases when the fringe period lambda^2/(2nd) < 100 nm. That gives d > 761 nm at 450 nm ('about 800' is close; the 400/450 pair aliases above 677 nm) and d > 1137 nm at 550 nm, matching the finding. The 800 nm row (95/142/199 nm periods) checks. The UI slider reaches 1500 (ui_state.rs:129) and the Thick preset is 1200 (ui_state.rs:154). The procedural thickness base*(1-drainage+noise) reaches those values. The foam shader repeats the 7-sample loop per fragment (bubble_instanced.wgsl:192-212). The ΔE values come from the finder's script and are unverified here. The mechanism and thresholds are confirmed.

findings.title: Procedural drainage gradient is upside down: film is thinnest at the bottom (normal.y = -1) although +Y is up
findings.claim: drainage = 0.4*(1 - normal.y)*0.5*(1+p) is 0 at the top (normal.y = +1) and 0.4-0.8 at the bottom (normal.y = -1). thickness = base*(1 - drainage + ...) is therefore largest at the top and smallest at the bottom. The camera uses +Y up (camera.rs:94, look_at_rh(..., Vec3::Y)). The code comment at :206 ('film collects at bottom') and README.md:48 ('The top drains faster, becoming thinner') both say the opposite of what the formula does. The same formula is in bubble_instanced.wgsl:327-328. This is independent of optics-01: two separate inversions.
findings.derivation: At normal.y=+1: (1-1)=0, so drainage=0 and thickness=base. At normal.y=-1: (1-(-1))*0.5 = 1, so drainage = 0.4(1+p) in [0.4, 0.8] and thickness = base*(0.6 down to 0.2), i.e. 300 down to 100 nm for base=500. Gravity drainage thins the top, and black film first appears at the apex. The formula should use (1 + normal.y), or equivalently subtract a term that grows with normal.y.
findings.impact: The vertical color-band order is reversed relative to a real draining bubble, and near-black regions (thickness < 30 nm with noise) would appear at the bottom rather than the top. This is a cross-dimension item (drainage), reported here because this formula sets the thickness that feeds the interference color.
findings.recommendation: Change (1.0 - normal.y) to (1.0 + normal.y) in both shaders, or ideally sample the GPU drainage buffer for the base thickness profile, as the compute shader already does. Confirm with the drainage-dimension auditor that the GPU drainage buffer's theta convention matches.

verification.reasoning: bubble.wgsl:207-208: drainage = 0.4*(1-normal.y)*0.5*(1+p). At normal.y=+1 this is 0. At normal.y=-1 it is 0.4(1+p), so 0.4-0.8, and :228 thickness = base*(1-drainage+...) is thinnest at the bottom. The vertex shader applies no rotation (bubble.wgsl:86-95, normal passed through), and the camera is +Y up (camera.rs:94 look_at_rh(..., Vec3::Y)). The comment at :206 and README.md:48 ('top drains faster, becoming thinner') contradict the formula. bubble_instanced.wgsl:327-328 is identical. Physical reference: Huang 2020 eq. (36) and §6.1 (PDF p.10), 'Soap films under the influence of gravity are thinner at the top and thicker at the bottom.' This is independent of optics-01.

findings.title: Screenshots/recordings swap R and B unconditionally; on the GL backend the chosen surface is Rgba8UnormSrgb
findings.claim: Both readback paths always swap bytes 0 and 2, assuming BGRA. The surface format is the first sRGB format the adapter reports (pipeline.rs:335-340). In wgpu-hal 24.0.4 the GLES backend lists Rgba8UnormSrgb before Bgra8UnormSrgb (gles/adapter.rs:1185-1194), so on the dev machine's WSLg GLES backend (#38) exported PNGs would have red and blue swapped. If supports_srgb() is false, the fallback is formats[0] = Rgba8Unorm: no sRGB encode at all, plus the swap.
findings.derivation: Code-read only, not measured. Format order in ~/.cargo/registry/.../wgpu-hal-24.0.4/src/gles/adapter.rs:1185-1194: formats = [Rgba8Unorm, Bgra8Unorm] extended with [Rgba8UnormSrgb, Bgra8UnormSrgb] when supports_srgb. Applying .find(is_srgb) picks Rgba8UnormSrgb. The same swap is at frame_exporter.rs:297-299. headless.rs (used by the golden tests) renders to Rgba8UnormSrgb and does not swap, so it is consistent.

findings.recommendation: Swap only when config.format is Bgra8Unorm or Bgra8UnormSrgb. Discriminator: log config.format once at pipeline.rs:340 on the WSLg machine.

findings.title: Polarization averaged before the Airy formula instead of after (up to 7.7% of peak error at oblique angles)
findings.claim: The code computes R = (Rs+Rp)/2 and then applies Airy(R). For unpolarized light the correct result is the average of Airy(Rs) and Airy(Rp), and the Airy function is nonlinear in R. Same at bubble.wgsl:450 and bubble_instanced.wgsl:198.
findings.code_quote: let fresnel = fresnel_unpolarized(cos_theta, cos_theta_t, 1.0, n_film);
findings.derivation: Exact per-polarization slab vs Airy(R_avg), both with the correct phase (airy_check.py [5]). cos_i=1: 0.0% (Rs=Rp). cos_i=0.6 (near Brewster, Rp~0): max error 0.0101 = 7.6% of peak. cos_i=0.3: 0.035 = 7.7%. cos_i=0.15: 2.5%. cos_i=0.05: 2.6%.
findings.impact: Small error, limited to the rim of the bubble. Free to fix in the precomputed LUT.
findings.recommendation: In the LUT generator, evaluate Airy separately with Rs and Rp and average the results.

findings.title: Hard 30 nm black-film cutoff creates a brightness and color step and becomes redundant once optics-01 is fixed
findings.claim: Below 30 nm the shader returns a constant 0.02 grey at alpha*0.5. This skips the 0.1*base_color term that the normal path adds at :532, and it skips the LUT. Physical reflectance is continuous: R(550 nm, 30 nm) = 0.0159, about 21% of the first-order peak. With the current phase bug the jump at 30 nm goes from sRGB (39,39,39) to (93,79,50) (DeltaE76 32 vs the continuous reference (34,41,50)). With the phase fixed, the Airy formula produces Newton's black naturally as d->0 (R(5 nm)=4.8e-4). The same cutoff is at bubble_instanced.wgsl:379-381.
findings.derivation: Exact R at 550 nm: d=5: 0.00048, 20: ~0.0072, 29.9: 0.01584, 30: 0.01593. The reference sRGB8 colors at 29.9 and 30.0 are both (34,41,50). The code path at 30.0 is (93,79,50) because of optics-01. Below 30 nm it outputs 0.02 with no base term (color_check.py [D]).
findings.impact: A visible contour at the 30 nm isoline. It currently also hides optics-01 in the thinnest regions.
findings.recommendation: After fixing optics-01, delete the branch, or keep it only as an opacity or rupture effect while letting the LUT supply the color.

findings.title: Opacity-style alpha blending instead of reflection plus transmission compositing (background dimmed 30% where physical T >= 92%)
findings.claim: With ALPHA_BLENDING (pipeline.rs:506), the output is src*alpha + dst*(1-alpha) with alpha = 0.3 + 0.6*smoothstep(1-cos). A lossless film reflects R(lambda) and transmits T = 1 - R(lambda): dst*T + R*L. At normal incidence R <= 0.077, so the background should keep at least 92% of its intensity, not 70%. The interference color is also scaled down by alpha.
findings.code_quote:
bubble.wgsl:513 let alpha = bubble.base_alpha + bubble.edge_alpha * smooth_edge;
pipeline.rs:506 blend: Some(wgpu::BlendState::ALPHA_BLENDING),
findings.derivation: Energy conservation for a non-absorbing film gives R + T = 1, with R_max(normal) = 4R0/(1+R0)^2 = 0.0771 for n=1.33. Default base_alpha=0.3 (pipeline.rs:78) attenuates dst by 0.7 at the center.
findings.impact: The bubble looks like a tinted semi-opaque shell rather than a nearly invisible film with colored reflections. This may be deliberate art direction.
findings.recommendation: If physical look is the goal, output premultiplied reflected RGB with alpha = R_avg and use PREMULTIPLIED_ALPHA_BLENDING, so that out = R_rgb + dst*(1-R_avg). Chromatic transmission would need dual-source blending. Expose base_alpha as an artistic override.

findings.title: Docs describe the obsolete model (Schlick, 3 RGB wavelengths, two-beam) and never state that the Airy delta excludes pi; the Born & Wolf summary gives reflection conditions that are wrong
findings.claim: (a) The Born & Wolf summary states 'Constructive: 2nd cos theta_t = m lambda (m = 0,1,2,...)' and 'Destructive: (m+1/2) lambda'. For reflection from a free-standing film these are swapped (they are the transmission conditions). It implies d=0 is bright, which is the same physics error as optics-01. (b) The code uses full s/p Fresnel, 7-sample CIE and Airy, but CLAUDE.md:48-49 ('Wavelengths: R=650nm, G=532nm, B=450nm', 'Fresnel reflection via Schlick approximation'), README.md:44, docs/physics-reference.md:49-59 (Schlick) and :138-159 (3 wavelengths, I=(1+cos phi)/2), and docs/key-insights.md:254-310 still describe Schlick, 3 RGB wavelengths and the two-beam form. docs/potential-improvements.md:60 says 'Fresnel ... Schlick approx', :100 says 'Current gap: Only 3 wavelengths', :206-213 says 'shader uses simpler formula', and :269 says 'Schlick approximation averages polarizations'; all are stale, and the doc's own log at :430-438/:531-625 contradicts them. (c) The comment at bubble.wgsl:376 says F is higher for 'thicker films'; F = 4R/(1-R)^2 depends only on the angle through R, not on thickness.
findings.code_quote:
references/Born_Wolf_1999_Principles_of_Optics_summary.md:65 $$2nd\cos\theta_t = m\lambda \quad (m = 0, 1, 2, ...)$$
CLAUDE.md:49 - Fresnel reflection via Schlick approximation
bubble.wgsl:376 // Higher F = sharper interference fringes (thicker films, grazing angles)
findings.derivation: From optics-01: R ~ sin^2(2 pi n d cos theta_t/lambda), so it is bright at 2nd cos theta_t = (m+1/2) lambda and dark at m lambda (m=0 is black film). docs/physics-reference.md:25-33 states the conditions using delta including lambda/2 and is correct. The B&W summary drops the lambda/2 but keeps the labels, which makes it wrong. The Airy formula in potential-improvements.md:206 and :490-493 leaves delta undefined, and the CPU code filled it with the lambda/2-inclusive OPD.
findings.impact: The stale docs send readers to a model that no longer exists. The B&W summary and the undefined delta in the Airy docs reproduce the conditions that caused the optics-01 regression.
findings.recommendation: Fix the B&W summary conditions (for reflection: bright at (m+1/2) lambda, dark at m lambda). Wherever the Airy formula appears, define delta = 4 pi n d cos theta_t/lambda without the pi, and explain why. Update CLAUDE.md, README and physics-reference to describe full Fresnel, Airy, the CIE LUT, and the LUT's format and range. Mark the potential-improvements.md items 2, 7 and 10 as done. Fix the bubble.wgsl:376 comment.

findings.title: LUT half-texel addressing offset (up to 3.9 nm thickness, 0.008 in cos theta)
findings.claim: Texel i stores d = i*2000/255 (interference_lut.rs:25-27). The shader samples u = d/2000, but under linear filtering texel i sits at (i+0.5)/256, so the effective thickness is d*256/255 - 3.92 nm.
findings.code_quote: let u = clamp(thickness_nm / LUT_MAX_THICKNESS_NM, 0.0, 1.0);
findings.derivation: texel_check.py: d=30 sampled as 26.2 (-3.8 nm, phase -0.159 rad at 400 nm); d=500 sampled as 498.0 (-2.0 nm); d=1500 sampled as 1502.0; cos 0.9 sampled as 0.906. The texel pitch is 7.84 nm, a 0.328 rad phase step at 400 nm, so linear interpolation is adequate.
findings.impact: Negligible next to the other findings.
findings.recommendation: Use u = (d/max*(N-1) + 0.5)/N, and the same for v. This can go in with the LUT format change.

findings.title: State-of-the-art gap: Belcour & Barla 2017 iridescence model (and Kneiphof et al. 2019 for IBL)
findings.claim: Belcour & Barla 2017 ('A Practical Extension to Microfacet Theory for the Modeling of Varying Iridescence', ACM TOG 36(4)) is the standard reference for real-time thin-film rendering. What this code is missing relative to it: (1) Airy reflectance with the phase handled per interface, including the phase of the Fresnel terms, so it also works when n_film < n_substrate; (2) per-polarization evaluation; (3) analytic spectral integration in the Fourier domain against Gaussian XYZ responses, which anti-aliases high-order fringes (optics-04); (4) consistent illuminant and white point (optics-03); (5) coupling to a microfacet BRDF or environment lighting (Kneiphof, Golla, Klein 2019 add IBL). Here the reflected color is effectively R(lambda) under an implied white light, with no environment term. The LUT also has a single mip level, so sub-pixel thickness variation is not prefiltered.
findings.derivation: From literature knowledge, not fetched in this session. The comparison against the code is by code-read.
findings.impact: The planned direction of the physically accurate claim. The cheapest and largest gains come from optics-01/03/04, all of which can be fixed inside the precomputed LUT.
findings.recommendation: Short term: rebuild the LUT with exact per-polarization Airy, CIE 1931 tables and D65 at 1-5 nm, store it as Rgba16Float, and have bubble_instanced.wgsl sample the same LUT. Longer term: environment-lit reflection in the Belcour-Barla style, and thickness-axis prefiltering (mip chain along u) for steep thickness gradients.

findings.title: CPU explicit-Euler drainage is unstable near the poles at default settings: no dt clamp, no sub-stepping, no CFL control
findings.claim: DrainageSimulator::step uses forward Euler with the raw frame dt times time_scale. At the default time_scale=100 and 60 fps that gives dt=1.667 s, 14.5 times the explicit diffusion limit of 0.115 s at theta ring 1. TFE fronts create phi-asymmetric perturbations, these reach the polar rings, and the scheme then blows up.
findings.derivation: Laplacian at drainage.rs:368-371: (1/R^2)[h_tt + cot(t) h_t + h_pp/sin^2(t)]. For forward Euler with central differences the worst Fourier mode (checkerboard) has lambda = 4D/(R^2 dth^2) + 4D/(R^2 sin^2(t) dph^2), and stability needs dt <= 2/lambda. Inputs: resolution=128 -> NT=128, NP=256, dth=pi/127=0.02474, dph=2pi/256=0.02454, R=0.025, D=fluid.surfactant_diffusion=1e-9 (drainage.rs:270). The theta direction alone allows dt <= R^2 dth^2/(2D) = 191 s. The 1/sin^2(t) factor at ring 1 (sin=0.0247, factor 1640) collapses this. Computed: dt_max(ring1)=0.1151 s, ring2=0.459 s, ring3=1.029 s, ring4=1.82 s. Default dt = (1/60)*100 = 1.667 s, so the per-step amplification at ring 1 is |1 - 1.667*17.38| = 28. Stability at 60 fps requires time_scale <= ~6.9; the slider range is 1..500 (ui_state.rs:327). Numerical replica (scratchpad/drainage/cpu_replica.py, trace_instab.py) reproduces step(), update_poles() and update_marginal_regeneration() line by line. The first ring-1 phi asymmetry appears at frame 18. At frame 24 ring 1 spans [0, 1353] nm; at frame 27 the maximum is 1.56e4 nm; by frame 80 (~1.3 s wall) 2034 cells are 0 and the pole is 0 nm. Control run with TFE off: stays bounded (499.6-500 nm), which confirms TFE is the seed. Frame hitch: a 0.5 s hitch gives dt=50 s and amplification ~869 per step for any existing polar asymmetry. In my hitch test no asymmetry had formed yet, and the newly spawned front advanced past 0.95*pi/2 and was culled in the same call, so that run alone did not blow up.
findings.impact: Within about 0.4 s of wall time after enabling 'Physics Drainage (CPU)', the thickness field near both poles contains spikes up to 30x the initial thickness, then a cap of zero-thickness cells. min_thickness()->0 drives bubble_uniform.drainage_speed=(1-min/max) to ~1 (pipeline.rs:1315), and the 'would burst' log fires every frame (pipeline.rs:1318-1323).
findings.recommendation: Sub-step inside step(): n = ceil(dt / (0.8*dt_max)), with dt_max computed once from the grid. Also clamp the frame dt (e.g. min(dt, 0.1 s)) before scaling. Better still: D*Laplacian(h) is physically negligible (R^2/D ~ 6e5 s), so treat the phi-diffusion implicitly (one periodic tridiagonal solve per ring, ADI), or apply polar Fourier filtering, or coarsen phi near the poles. Any of these removes the 1/sin^2 stiffness.

verification.reasoning: Verified: forward Euler at drainage.rs:380, with pipeline.rs:1296-1297 passing dt*drainage_time_scale (default 100, pipeline.rs:802) and no clamp on frame dt (main.rs:172). findings.title: GPU drainage never changes the thickness field: params.dt is never updated and the 1 ms update is below f32 resolution
findings.claim: step() computes step_dt but only uses it to advance current_time. The shader always uses params.dt = 0.001 from DrainageParams::default, because set_dt/update_params/set_physics have no callers. At h=500 nm in f32 the per-step decrement is 0.007 ulp, so h is rounded back to itself. A uniform start has zero Laplacian and zero grad(Gamma), and nothing else writes the buffer. So the thickness buffer read by branched flow and caustics stays at exactly 500 nm forever, the time_scale and steps sliders only change the displayed 'Sim time', and Marangoni has nothing to act on.
findings.code_quote:
let step_dt = scaled_dt / self.steps_per_frame as f32;   // gpu_drainage.rs:355 (never written to params)
self.current_time += step_dt as f64;   // gpu_drainage.rs:376
dt: 0.001,                 // 1ms time step   // gpu_drainage.rs:49
let new_h = max(h + params.dt * dh_dt, 0.0);   // drainage.wgsl:179
findings.derivation: rg 'set_dt|set_physics|set_bubble_radius|update_params' finds only the definitions in gpu_drainage.rs (385-416); pipeline.rs never calls them. In the shader, drainage_coeff = rho*g/(3*eta) = 3.27e6 and h^3 = 1.25e-19 (a normal f32, no denormal issue), so |dt*dh/dt| <= 0.001*4.09e-13 = 4.09e-16 m. ulp(f32 5e-7) = 5.684e-14 m, so the ratio is 0.0072 ulp, below half an ulp even with FMA. Numerical check (scratchpad/drainage/f32_check.py): 0 of 126 interior rows change after one step. For a uniform field, d2h and dh are exactly 0, so the Laplacian is 0; concentration is uniform 0.5, so the Marangoni term is 0 and dc_dt is 0. Pole rows are copied unchanged. rg over shaders shows thickness is read-only in caustics_compute.wgsl:25 and branched_flow_compute.wgsl:68; the only writers are drainage.wgsl:34 and the uniform reset (gpu_drainage.rs:428-437). By induction the field stays bitwise uniform. Wiring set_dt to the intended step_dt=(1/60*100)/10=0.167 s would still be quantized: 92 of 126 rows decrement by exactly 1 ulp, and the true decrement of 0-1.2 ulp is lost to rounding. That dt would also exceed the 0.115 s diffusion limit (drainage-01) at ring 1.
findings.impact: Ray bending from the GRIN thickness gradient in branched flow (thickness_gradient_uv, branched_flow_compute.wgsl:268) and the caustic gradient/Laplacian are identically zero, so every branched-flow structure comes from scatterers. Visual verification of #26 and the #39 discussion are therefore based on a flat field. Ten compute passes of 32k cells per frame do no useful work (cost on real GPU [estimated, requires measurement]; on llvmpipe (#38) pure overhead). The GPU 'Sim time' label advances 100x real time while the physics does not move.
findings.recommendation: Write params.dt = step_dt once per frame (queue.write_buffer before the passes), and pick steps_per_frame from the CFL limit rather than a slider. Store a nondimensional deviation (h/h0 - 1, or h in units of h0 with a separate f32 delta) so per-step changes are many ulps. Start from a non-uniform state, e.g. Huang 2020's equilibrium eta ~ exp(-g cos(theta)/M), so gradients exist. Record the 10 sub-steps as dispatches in a single compute pass; wgpu tracks per-dispatch usage in compute passes [estimated benefit].

findings.title: Gravity-drainage term has the wrong units, does not conserve mass, and is symmetric about the equator (bottom never thickens, top pole never thins)
findings.claim: The term actually implemented, dh/dt = -(rho g/(3 eta)) h^3 sin(theta), is the magnitude of a volume flux (m^2/s), not the divergence of one (m/s). It is <= 0 everywhere, symmetric about the equator, largest at the equator and zero at the poles. The code comment claims 'top thins, bottom thickens', which this form cannot produce. The GPU shader has the identical term.
findings.derivation: Units: [rho g/eta] = (kg m^-2 s^-2)/(kg m^-1 s^-1) = m^-1 s^-1, so [rho g h^3/eta] = m^2/s, which cannot be added to dh/dt [m/s]; a 1/length (the 1/R of the surface divergence) is missing. Lubrication on a sphere with R >> h and tangential gravity g sin(theta) e_theta: with rigid (no-slip, surfactant-laden) interfaces the Poiseuille flux is q = rho g sin(theta) h^3/(12 eta). The 3*eta coefficient is the film-on-substrate case (one no-slip and one free surface). Mass conservation gives h_t = -(1/(R sin t)) d_t(sin t * q) = -(rho g/(12 eta R)) (1/sin t) d_t(sin^2 t h^3). For uniform h this is -(rho g h^3/(6 eta R)) cos(theta), which is antisymmetric. Checked numerically (scratchpad/drainage/pde_compare.py): the finite-difference divergence matches the analytic form to 1.6e-6. Rates at h=500 nm: top pole, code 0 vs conservative -8.18e-3 nm/s; equator, code -4.09e-4 vs 0; bottom pole, code 0 vs +8.18e-3 nm/s. Net volume rate: code -2.52e-15 m^3/s, equal to the analytic -(rho g h^3/3eta) pi^2 R^2; conservative form 3e-30, i.e. zero. The magnitudes differ by 1/(2R) = 20. The physical reference in the repo, Huang 2020's equilibrium eta ~ exp(-g cos(theta)/M) (references/Huang_2020_..._summary.md), is thinner at the top and thicker at the bottom with total volume conserved; the code's model has no such steady state. Other mass errors: max(0) at :380 injects mass when it clips; cells below the critical thickness are frozen (:326) while their neighbours still diffuse against them.
findings.impact: Wrong thickness map: the equator band thins fastest, the top pole (where real bubbles first turn black) stays thickest, the bottom never accumulates, and the total film volume decreases monotonically. Interference colours driven by this field would have the wrong vertical structure.
findings.recommendation: Replace it with a conservative finite-volume form on the sphere: face fluxes q_{i+1/2} = rho g sin(theta_{i+1/2}) h^3_{i+1/2}/(12 eta), with zero flux through the pole faces and dh_i/dt = -(sin t_{i+1/2} q_{i+1/2} - sin t_{i-1/2} q_{i-1/2})/(R sin t_i dth). Either document 12*eta as the rigid-interface choice or adopt Huang 2020's (u, eta, Gamma) surface-flow model, which captures mobile interfaces. Explicit stability for this hyperbolic term is a CFL condition dt <= R dth / u_max with u_max = 3 rho g h^2/(12 eta); this is very permissive here.

verification.reasoning: drainage.rs:346 and drainage.wgsl:136 compute -ρg h^3 sinθ/(3η). Units: (kg m^-3 · m s^-2)/(Pa s) · m^3 = m^2/s, a flux, not dh/dt. The term is ≤ 0 everywhere and symmetric about the equator, so the comment at :341-344 ('top thins, bottom thickens') is false. Re-derived the conservative form: h_t = -(1/(R sinθ)) ∂θ(sinθ q). With q = ρg sinθ h^3/(12η) and uniform h, h_t = -(ρg h^3/(6ηR)) cosθ, which is antisymmetric. At h=500 nm that is 8.18e-3 nm/s at the poles against the code's 4.09e-4 nm/s at the equator. Ratio 1/(2R) = 20 for 12η, or 2/R = 80 for 3η as in sota-05. Code net volume rate: -c·R^2·2π·∫sin^2 = -cπ^2R^2 = -2.52e-15 m^3/s, which checks. Huang 2020 eq. (36) gives a top-thin/bottom-thick equilibrium. Downgraded to medium because the term's effect is negligible in practice: about 4e-4 nm/s, swamped by TFE on CPU (drainage-04) and lost below f32 resolution on GPU (drainage-02). The model is still wrong and should be fixed. Duplicate of sota-05.

findings.title: 'TFE ratio 0.85 (Monier 2025)' is applied as unbounded exponential decay; goes negative for dt > 13.3 s and turns the equator black within seconds
findings.claim: Monier et al. report a bounded thickness ratio of 0.8-0.9 between thin-film elements and the adjacent film. The code instead multiplies h by (1 - 0.075*dt) every step a cell is inside a front, which is exponential decay with no target or floor. This runs after the PDE's max(0) clamp, so for dt > 1/0.075 = 13.3 s the factor is negative and thickness goes negative.
findings.code_quote:
let reduction_rate = (1.0 - self.tfe_thickness_ratio) * 0.5; // per second
let new_thickness = current * (1.0 - reduction_rate * dt);   // drainage.rs:456-457
findings.derivation: Inside a front, h(t) = h0 * prod(1 - 0.075 dt) ~ h0 exp(-0.075 t): 0.86 at 2 s, 0.47 at 10 s, 0.105 at 30 s, 0.011 at 60 s. A front lives ~15-30 s (1.49 rad at 0.05-0.1 rad/s, drainage.rs:471, :414), up to 8 overlap, and they spawn every 1-3 s. Replica at a stable dt=0.1 s for 60 s of sim time (0.6 s wall at time_scale 100): equator (phi=0) = 11.8 nm, below the 30 nm black-film threshold. Negative path, replica neg_check.py: dt=15 s gives min -62.5 nm in 3120 cells at frame 1; dt=20 s gives -250 nm. dt >= 13.3 s happens at time_scale 100 below 7.5 fps (plausible on the llvmpipe dev box, #38) or at time_scale 500 below 37.5 fps. Negative cells fall below critical_thickness, so the PDE skips them (:326) and they stay negative; base_thickness_nm takes the equator value (pipeline.rs:1306-1310). Physics: the arXiv 2511.08194 abstract says 'thin film elements (TFEs)' 'formed at the meniscus' with ratio 0.8-0.9. A free bubble has no meniscus at its equator, and the code spawns fronts at the equator spreading symmetrically to both poles. The code's doc calls it a 'Thick Film Element' (drainage.rs:20).
findings.impact: The visible behaviour of CPU drainage is dominated by this ad-hoc sink, not by the PDE; the gravity term is ~4e-4 nm/s. The equator goes black almost immediately, mass is removed without limit, and at low fps or high time_scale the thickness becomes negative.
findings.recommendation: Relax towards a bounded target: h <- h + (ratio*h_adjacent - h)*(1 - exp(-dt/tau)), using exp so it stays stable for any dt, with h_adjacent taken from outside the front or a stored base field. Spawn TFEs at a meniscus/boundary that makes sense for the geometry (e.g. the bottom for a bubble on a bath) and move them upward (buoyant). Rename to 'thin film element'.

verification.reasoning: drainage.rs:456-457: reduction_rate = (1-0.85)*0.5 = 0.075/s and new = current*(1-0.075 dt), with no target or floor. It runs after the PDE's max(0) (:380, then :390), so the factor is negative for dt > 13.33 s. At time_scale 100 that is a frame dt ≥ 0.133 s (< 7.5 fps). Negative cells fall below critical (10 nm) and are skipped by the PDE (:326), so they persist. Exponential decay e^{-0.075t} gives 0.47 at 10 s and 0.011 at 60 s, which checks. Front lifetime is 1.49 rad at 0.05-0.1 rad/s, i.e. 15-30 s. The spawn φ = |sin(...)|·2π (:469) has an arcsine distribution concentrated near 0 and 2π (both φ≈0), which plausibly explains the heavy coverage of the φ=0 equator sample that pipeline.rs:1305-1310 uses as base_thickness_nm. The doc calls it 'Thick Film Element' (:20) while describing thin regions (:21). The 11.8 nm and -62.5 nm replica values were not reproduced here. The arXiv citation is unverified. Opt-in CPU path, so high rather than critical.

The GPU solver is constructed with literal values and DrainageParams::default(), and both resets hard-code 500 nm. So --thickness, --diameter, --config fluid values and critical_thickness_nm have no effect on drainage. The critical thickness also differs: 10 nm in config, 30 nm on the GPU.

                self.init_drainage_simulator(&config);   // pipeline.rs:1749-1750
self.reset_drainage(500.0);   // pipeline.rs:1754
&device, 500e-9, // Initial thickness: 500nm   // pipeline.rs:709
self.gpu_drainage.reset(&self.queue, 500e-9);   // pipeline.rs:1781
critical_thickness: 30e-9, // 30nm critical thickness   // gpu_drainage.rs:55
findings.derivation: rg shows sim_config is used only at pipeline.rs:375-376 and :645, and is not stored for later use. set_physics and set_bubble_radius (gpu_drainage.rs:397-416) have no callers. config.rs:31 sets critical_thickness_nm=10.0, while the GPU default is 30e-9. findings.title: GPU pole rows are frozen (Dirichlet at the initial value), not averaged; the in-code comment and key-insights.md say otherwise
findings.claim: Rows theta=0 and theta=pi are copied unchanged every step. average_poles was removed, so the poles stay at their initial value forever and ring 1 sees a pinned neighbour. The CPU solver averages ring 1 into the pole (drainage.rs:483-506), so CPU and GPU boundary conditions differ.
findings.derivation: No other kernel writes the pole rows, and get_thickness clamps the theta index (wgsl:48), so the Laplacian at ring 1 uses h_pole = h_initial. In correct physics (drainage-03) the top pole thins fastest; a pinned pole would hold it at the starting thickness. This is latent today because the GPU field is invariant (drainage-02), but it becomes visible once that is fixed. The comment 'averaging done separately' at :84 contradicts :208-211. docs/key-insights.md:770 says 'Special handling at poles: averaged from neighboring ring'.
findings.impact: After the dt fix the top cap could never thin, and colours near the poles would be wrong. The docs give a false picture of the boundary condition.
findings.recommendation: Use the finite-volume form with zero pole flux (drainage-03 recommendation), which needs no special pole row. Or average ring 1 into the pole in a second tiny dispatch with its own ping-pong. Fix the comment at :84 and key-insights.md:770.

verification.reasoning: drainage.wgsl:84-89 copies pole rows unchanged, and :208-211 states that average_poles was removed. The ':84 averaging done separately' comment is therefore false. get_thickness clamps θ (:48), so ring 1 always sees the initial pole value. The CPU averages ring 1 into the poles (drainage.rs:483-506), so the boundary conditions differ between CPU and GPU. docs/key-insights.md:770 says 'averaged from neighboring ring', which is doc drift. This is latent while the GPU field is invariant (drainage-02), hence low.

findings.title: Marangoni coupling has no consistent units, is a one-signed source term, and does nothing in practice
findings.claim: marangoni_term = coeff*gamma_r*|grad Gamma|*h^2 has units N (times an unspecified coeff). It is always >= 0, so it is a mass source, not a divergence. The concentration feedback 0.001*h_laplacian*R^2 has units of metres and is added to dGamma/dt. With uniform initial h and Gamma, both terms are exactly zero, so toggling 'Marangoni effect' changes nothing.
findings.code_quote:
marangoni_term = params.marangoni_coeff * marangoni_stress * h * h;   // wgsl:174
let thickness_gradient_coupling = 0.001 * (h_laplacian * params.bubble_radius * params.bubble_radius);   // wgsl:200
findings.derivation: [gamma_r]=N/m, [|grad Gamma|]=1/m (Gamma is dimensionless), [h^2]=m^2, so the product is N. To give m/s, marangoni_coeff would need units m/(N s); the doc says 'M/eta' (gpu_drainage.rs:39), which does not have those units. The correct Marangoni-driven flux is q = (h^2/(2 eta)) grad(gamma) (or plug flow for a symmetric film), with h_t = -div q, which conserves mass and has either sign. [h_laplacian*R^2] = m, so dc_dt gets units m/s and not 1/s. Even with a perturbation: a 1 nm thickness bump gives h_lap*R^2 ~ 1e-9/6e-4 = 1.6e-6, so the Gamma increment per step is ~0.001*0.001*1.6e-6*0.5 = 8e-13, far below ulp(0.5) = 6e-8, and is absorbed. The code comment at :170-173 acknowledges the scalar-magnitude simplification.
findings.impact: The UI offers a 'Surfactant-driven flow' toggle and strength slider (ui_state.rs:361-369) that have no effect. If they did act, they would only ever thicken the film.
findings.recommendation: Implement Huang 2020's conservative coupled system: Gamma_t + div(Gamma u) = D_s Lap(Gamma), with u driven by -grad(gamma)/eta-type terms, and h_t + div(h u) = 0. Use consistent SI units and state them in DrainageParams docs.

verification.reasoning: drainage.wgsl:165-174: grad_c_mag is a sqrt, so it is ≥ 0. gamma_reduction is 0.045 and marangoni_coeff 0.01 (gpu_drainage.rs:61,63), so marangoni_term ≥ 0 always and acts as a source. Units: [N/m]·[1/m]·[m^2] = N, as the finding says. :200: h_laplacian [1/m]·R^2 = m, added to dΓ/dt. With uniform initial h and Γ both terms are exactly 0, so the toggle (ui_state.rs:364) does nothing. My arithmetic also gives 8e-13 for the perturbation estimate, well below ulp(0.5) = 6e-8. The code comment at :170-173 admits the always-thickening simplification. Partially overlaps drainage-02.

findings.title: Ping-pong output accessor returns the buffer read in the last step (one step stale); the comment has the parity backwards
findings.claim: After a step with bind_groups[k] (reads buffers[k], writes buffers[1-k]), current_buffer is flipped to 1-k, which is the buffer just written. current_buffer() returns thickness_buffers[1 - current_buffer] = buffers[k], the buffer that was read. Consumers get a state one sub-step old. concentration_buffer() (:490) has the same parity. There is no read/write race.
findings.derivation: Trace: start cb=0 -> set_bind_group(bind_groups[0]) = A->B, which writes buffers[1] (:251-258) -> cb = 1 (:375). The next input is buffers[cb]=buffers[1], which is the newest output. The accessor returns buffers[1-1]=buffers[0], the stale input. With steps_per_frame=10, branched flow (rebuild_bind_group, pipeline.rs:1424-1428) sees step 9 of 10; with steps=1 it sees the previous frame. Caustics is bound once at init to buffers[1] (pipeline.rs:722; caustics.rs:212-222 never rebuilt), so it alternates between fresh and stale depending on step parity. Bind groups are correct: no buffer is bound read and read_write in the same pass.
findings.impact: Small one-step lag; latent while the field is invariant (drainage-02). The inverted comment invites future mistakes.
findings.recommendation: Return &self.thickness_buffers[self.current_buffer] (and the same for concentration), and fix the comment. Rebuild the caustics bind group per frame as is done for branched flow, or use two pre-built bind groups indexed by parity.

findings.title: Drainage docs are dimensionally wrong, internally contradictory, and stale on roadmap status, pole BC, grid size and TFE naming
findings.claim: The documented drainage equation has inconsistent units and does not match the code. The doc set gives three incompatible scaling laws (h^3/(3eta), h^2/(3eta) attributed to Monier, h^2/eta). Status tables still list implemented features as missing. Pole handling, grid size and TFE naming are wrong.
findings.code_quote:
∂d/∂t = -ρgd³/(3η) + D∇²d + Marangoni terms   (docs/physics-reference.md:112)
dh/dt ∝ -ρgh²/(3η) with gravity scaling   (docs/potential-improvements.md:481)
